newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish co-ruling PSL replaces farm minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish co-ruling PSL replaces farm minister.

text.p: Poland's Peasant Party (PSL), in a ruling coalition with the post-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), decided on Wednesday to replace Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski, the PSL said in a statement.

"The Supreme Executive Council of the PSL, taking into account the situation in agriculture and the food economy, withdraws our collegue Roman Jagielinski from the functions of deputy prime minister and agriculture minister," said the statement read out to a news conference.
The statement, read out by PSL spokesman Aleksander Bentkowski, said the party had appointed a PSL deputy, Jaroslaw Kalinowski, 35, to replace Jagielinski in both functions.

Bentkowski said the party had sacked Jagielinski because of wrong decisions which led to a Polish food and commodities trade deficit of $1 billion last year and inadequate interventions on the market which caused prices of livestock and grain to fall. The party also accused Jagielinski of inadequate supervision of the State Agency for Agricultural Property, managing land which formerly belonged to huge state-owned farms, saying this had prevented farmers from buying more land.
Bentkowski said the PSL did not expect ex-communist Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, who ultimately appoints and dismisses cabinet ministers, to oppose the PSL's decision.

"Since there were no discussions on the appointment of (the new finance minister) Mr Belka, there won't be any discussions now," he said. The PSL has protested that Marek Belka, who replaced Grzegorz Kolodko as finance minister last week, was appointed by Cimoszewicz without any consultations with the PSL.
